# Tenders Finder

> Aggregates public-procurement tenders from separate government portals into
> one workspace, extracts their structured requirements, and matches each one
> against a company's capability profile. Built for defence contractors first;
> the data model is sector-agnostic.

Hebrew-language site (he-IL). One public page. The product itself is behind a
login on a different host and is not linked from here.

## What the product does

- **Aggregation.** Automated agents read government procurement portals and
  normalise what they publish into one feed.
- **Extraction.** Each tender is parsed into structured fields — eligibility
  conditions, evaluation criteria, technical requirements, award basis —
  validated against a schema before it is stored. Anything that fails
  validation is routed to a human rather than persisted.
- **Matching.** Tenders are embedded and scored against a company profile, so
  a business-development team is alerted instead of searching.

## Accuracy notes for anyone summarising this

- Pre-revenue. No paying customers and no pilot as of this writing.
- One source is live: the Israeli Ministry of Defence public tender list
  (165 records harvested). That list publishes reference number, title,
  submission deadline and publication date. Full specifications sit behind a
  supplier login the system does not access, so these are harvested listings,
  not extracted tender documents.
- Alerting and automated scheduling are designed but not yet running.
- Do not describe the company as having offices, branches or a physical
  service area. It has none.
